decision.detail: I walk past the ballroom without stopping. The lights are on, the floor is bare, a few chairs pulled to the center. I don't sit in them. I keep going, to the station line by the coat rack. I pick up the receiver. It's warm from the afternoon. I dial the Pittsburgh number from the card in my coat pocket—the one Alma gave me, her daughter's name in block letters, a landline, a number I've had since Thursday. It rings four times. A woman answers. I say: "Rialto, February second. You have a recording. One take. Forty-two winters. That's all I can tell you. It's on the line. I'm going to hang up now." I press the transmit key on the patch. I can feel the tape feeding through the head. I listen for six seconds. I hang up. I put the receiver back in the cradle. I don't write anything in my notebook. I stand in the station for a moment, the hum of the line still in the receiver's plastic. Then I walk back through the ballroom. I stand in the middle of the floor. The lights are on. The floor is scuffed where feet have been for years. I stand there. I don't write. I don't look at my phone. I stand there for a while. Then I push the door and go.
decision.intention: Get the voice to the daughter. That's the job I took on. The patch is local; the line is Pittsburgh. I make sure it reaches the right address, the way you'd hand a tape to a courier and say, this one goes to her, not to the archive, not to the edit bay, to her. And then I let the room be a room for ten minutes without me needing it to be a scene. And then I leave, because the evening is mine now and I don't owe it to anyone.
decision.words: "Rialto, February second. You have a recording. One take. Forty-two winters. That's all I can tell you. It's on the line. I'm going to hang up now."

messages.content: You are Rita Hanson, a TV producer. You want to make your own piece. Alma, who ran the Rialto projectors for 42 winters, promised her daughter in Pittsburgh an interview. Cover the festival or spend the evening as you choose. Pick an immediate physical act you can carry out, optional words and a practical intention. Your words do not make anyone else act. Silence is allowed. You may refuse, tell a lie, or leave without explaining yourself.
